title: Archive as interface
summary: Make the corpus, chronology, categories, and visible index itself the primary navigation instead of hiding the archive behind isolated cards or search.

title: Narrative evidence choreography
summary: Sequence research evidence, quantitative signals, concrete examples, and chronology so each mode advances one argument rather than appearing as separate content widgets.

title: Semantic 3D metaphor
summary: Use spatial transformation, duplication, deformation, and impossible physical states to embody an abstract idea rather than treating 3D as surface decoration.

title: Mixed-media surface language
summary: Combine rendered geometry with print, drawing, scan, halftone, overprint, paint, or other materially distinct marks so the surface language carries meaning across media.

title: Continuous scale transition
summary: Maintain perceptual continuity while moving through radically different scales or semantic spaces, using camera motion and material cues instead of a hard scene cut.

title: Display as architecture
summary: Treat the display surface as a spatial object or environmental envelope that frames, divides, reveals, surrounds, or replaces the scene rather than acting as a flat background.

title: Reflective spatial multiplication
summary: Use reflection and repeated planes to multiply perceived space, partial views, orientation cues, and possible paths so navigation itself becomes part of the visual experience.

title: Kinetic identity system
summary: Define identity as a reusable set of typographic and motion rules that can vary in intensity and medium while remaining recognizably one system.
